## About

I started where most frontend developers start: turning designs into interfaces. What changed things was discovering that the interface is usually the smallest part of the problem. Behind almost every screen someone is retyping data that a machine could have read.

So I went looking for the layer underneath. n8n gave me a way to connect language models to real systems — documents in, validated structured data out, straight into the tools a business already uses. Arabic is where this gets interesting, because most global tools quietly do not handle it, and the region is moving fast toward mandatory digital invoicing.

I still write the frontend. I lead it, in fact — I set the standards, review the code, and mentor the developers. The difference is that I now design the whole path, from the moment a document arrives to the moment someone approves it on screen.

The other half of the job is coordination. I gather requirements directly from clients, define scope and acceptance criteria, break work into tasks, and keep delivery on schedule across frontend, backend, and design. It is less glamorous than the AI part and it is often what decides whether a project ships.

## How he works

### Agree the contract before the first line of code

The worst bug I have shipped was not in anyone's code. Two systems each behaved perfectly and disagreed about what a payload meant, so data deleted itself silently — no error, no log, nothing broken. Now every shared boundary gets a written agreement first: the shape of the data, the required fields, the strange cases, and who owns what. It lets two people build in parallel and still fit together on the first try.

### Accuracy before speed

A workflow that saves nothing is better than one that saves the wrong thing. My extraction pipelines refuse to persist anything until the essential fields are present and plausible — and when something is missing, they say so and explain why. A confident wrong answer is worse than a slow right one.

### Route by cost, not by habit

My first workflow sent every incoming file to a vision model. But a PDF usually carries extractable text, and a text model reads it for a fraction of the price. One branching decision cut the per-document cost by three quarters — with a fallback to vision when extraction comes back empty. The branch is free; the saving compounds every month.

### Build the thing people will actually open

An automation nobody trusts gets bypassed. A dashboard nobody understands gets exported to a spreadsheet. So I care about the interface as much as the pipeline: clear states, honest errors, and no dead ends.

## Projects

### Smart Scanner (2026)

*AI SaaS product* — Arabic-first AI invoice management — from photo to approval, with zero manual data entry.

**Problem.** In most companies an invoice sleeps in a pocket or a drawer until month-end, when a stack of paper lands on the accountant's desk to be typed in by hand. The result is lost time, human error, duplicate and forged invoices slipping through unnoticed, and no record of who submitted what. Global tools mostly cannot read an Arabic invoice at all.

**What he built.** I built two of the three layers: the entire AI extraction engine in n8n, and the complete frontend. The frontend is three role-based applications — admin, accountant, and employee — sharing one React 19 and TypeScript codebase, with an Arabic-default bilingual UI, full RTL through logical CSS properties, and a custom i18n layer. It includes a guided upload flow with in-page camera capture, a receipt browser with server-side filtering, Excel export, and feature gating across subscription tiers, all shipped through GitHub Actions quality gates and atomic SSH deploys.

**Role.** AI/automation engine and complete frontend. Laravel backend by Haitham Zedan.

**Numbers.** 204 source files · 494 automated tests · 70+ fields extracted · 13+ server-side filters · 4 subscription tiers · ~10s photo to structured data

**Stack.** React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Vitest, React Testing Library, n8n, OpenAI GPT-4.1 Vision, GitHub Actions, i18n, RTL

**Live.** https://receipt.nexleadtech.com

**Context.** Timed with the e-invoicing expansion in Saudi Arabia and mandatory JoFotara in Jordan — every paper invoice in the region now has to become clean digital data.

### CV Screener (2026)

*AI SaaS product* — Upload a folder of CVs — every one is read, classified, and scored by AI, with each point traced to a quote from the CV.

**Problem.** HR teams receive hundreds of CVs per opening, many of them Arabic PDFs that most tools cannot read. Screening them by hand is slow and inconsistent, and an AI score with no explanation is not something a recruiter can trust or defend.

**What he built.** A full-stack, Arabic-default bilingual product. HR uploads files, folders, or ZIPs; a background worker extracts the text — repairing Arabic visual order — and n8n profiles each CV, places it in the account's own categories, and scores it on several dimensions with quoted evidence. The server verifies every quote against the CV before it can raise a score, and computes every number people sort by. On top sit filters on every profile field, Arabic and English full-text search, HR status, stars and notes, role screenings with weighted criteria and must-haves, AI summaries of any scope, CSV export, and an admin console.

**Role.** Full build — product, frontend, backend, and AI workflows

**Numbers.** 1,189 automated tests · 8 scoring dimensions · 3 n8n AI workflows · 5,000 CVs performance-tested

**Stack.** Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Prisma, MySQL 8, n8n, OpenAI, Docker, Vitest, i18n, RTL

**Live.** https://cv-screener.nouraldeentofi.com

### Universal Web Scraper (2026)

*AI automation product* — One link in, the whole site out — every page discovered, the data classified, and an Excel file with a tab for each kind of data.

**Problem.** Collecting data from websites usually means copying it by hand into Excel, or writing a new scraper for every site — and breaking it the moment a site blocks bots or renders its content with JavaScript.

**What he built.** You paste one link. The engine discovers every page of the site through its sitemap, classifies what it finds — companies, people, products, articles, jobs, places — and fills an Excel file with a tab per category, mirrored to Google Sheets. It runs in the background on n8n, so it keeps going after the laptop is closed, and the rows collected so far can be downloaded at any moment; large sites are split into parts. Each page fetch escalates only as far as it needs — direct request, proxy pool, scraping API, full renderer — and extraction reads JSON-LD and tables first, falling back to chunked, parallel AI extraction. A small web interface shows live progress, a time estimate, a preview of the rows, and pause, resume, cancel, and restart controls.

**Role.** Full build — interface and automation

**Numbers.** 1 link to scrape a whole site · 7 data categories, one Excel tab each · 4 fetch tiers, escalated on demand

**Stack.** n8n, OpenAI, Excel, Google Sheets, JSON-LD, Sitemap crawling, Proxy pool, Webhooks, JavaScript

### Business Card Extractor (2026)

*AI web app* — Photograph a business card, and it lands in your phone's contacts in one tap.

**Problem.** You collect a stack of business cards at an event and never open it again. It is a small problem that quietly costs sales teams real pipeline.

**What he built.** A web app that turns a photo of any business card into structured data — name, company, email, phone, website — in seconds, stores it in Google Sheets, and generates a vCard so the contact saves straight to the phone. No custom backend at all: an n8n workflow receives the image, GPT-4o Vision reads it, the data is validated and stored, and it flows back to the app. The one-tap save came from a user suggestion after the first release.

**Role.** Full build — frontend and automation

**Numbers.** 0 lines of custom backend · 1 tap to save a contact

**Stack.** React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, n8n, OpenAI GPT-4o Vision, Google Sheets, vCard

### MCP Search Server (2026)

*AI tooling* — A Model Context Protocol server that lets an AI model query real data instead of only generating text.

**Problem.** Language models are fluent but disconnected. MCP is the bridge — but most of the discussion about it stays theoretical.

**What he built.** I built an MCP server with custom tools including a search tool, wired it to real data, and connected it to Claude — so a plain-language question like "what are the details of user 2" returns the correct record directly. The same pattern powers the MCP server that ships with this portfolio.

**Role.** Full build

**Numbers.** MCP tools exposed to Claude

**Stack.** Model Context Protocol, Node.js, Claude, JSON Schema

## Automation systems

### Universal Web Scraper (2026)

*AI scraping engine* — Live — 7 n8n workflow(s) — trigger: Web app (webhook) and a crawl schedule

**Flow.** Scrape job API → Crawl worker tick → Plan the job → Quick batch loop → Escalating fetch → Needs AI? → AI field extraction → Collect rows → Dedupe and merge → Excel and Sheets

One link in, the whole site out. A shared engine fetches pages and escalates only as far as it must, reads structured data before it spends anything on AI, and writes the rows into a spreadsheet — with quick jobs and long crawls run as separate, controllable workers.

**Services.** n8n, OpenAI, Google Sheets, Excel, n8n Data Tables, Webhooks

- One engine, called as a sub-workflow by both the quick runner and the crawl worker
- The AI call is skipped entirely when structured data already answers the page
- The crawl worker locks each job, opens a new sheet when a part fills up, and writes one tab per category
- Pause, resume, cancel, restart and delete, routed through a single control endpoint

**Outcome.** Collecting a website into Excel stops being copy-and-paste or a new script per site.

### CV Screener agents (2026)

*AI agents behind a product* — Live — 4 n8n workflow(s) — trigger: Server-to-server webhook

**Flow.** CV request webhook → Secret header check → Validate and fence → Valid request? → Profile the CV → Reject request → Structural check → Return JSON

The AI engine of CV Screener: sibling agents that profile one CV, screen one CV against a job, and summarise a whole pool. The product server calls them; every one checks a secret first, fences the CV as data, and returns typed JSON or a typed error.

**Services.** n8n, OpenAI, Webhooks, Structured outputs

- A secret header is checked before anything else; a bad call never reaches the model
- The CV text is wrapped in random fences, so instructions hidden inside a CV are read as data
- The model scores with quoted evidence; weighted totals and must-have caps are computed in code
- Set not to store executions, because CVs are personal data

**Outcome.** Hundreds of CVs become a ranked, explainable pool that a recruiter can defend.

*Telegram AI agent · client project* — Running for a client — 5 n8n workflow(s) — trigger: Telegram message

**Flow.** Telegram message → Verify the request → Shared a contact? → Capture the lead → Usage gate → Alert the owner → Limit reached → Teacher AI agent → Reply in chat

A natural-language Arabic assistant delivered to a private tutor in Saudi Arabia. The tutor manages students, schedules, cancellations, and dues entirely through chat — the AI agent calls custom CRUD tools under strict business rules rather than guessing.

**Services.** n8n AI Agent, OpenAI, Google Sheets, MySQL, Telegram Bot API, Webhooks

- Custom tool-calling design with strict business rules
- Usage metering and free-trial gating
- Session memory across conversations
- Automated lesson reminders scheduled in Saudi time
- Grew in stages: fixed commands without AI, then an AI agent, then a MySQL version with stored procedures as tools

**Outcome.** A tutor runs an entire practice from a chat window, with no app to learn and no spreadsheet to maintain.

### Smart Scanner Extraction Pipeline (2026)

*Production document AI pipeline* — Live — 1 n8n workflow(s) — trigger: Webhook (image or PDF upload)

**Flow.** Receipt upload → Secret header check → PDF or image? → Read the PDF → Read the image → Parse and validate → Valid receipt? → Reply to app → Reject and clean up → Post to backend

The production pipeline behind Smart Scanner. Every invoice — photo or PDF — is verified as a real invoice, parsed with GPT-4.1 Vision, validated, deduplicated, and persisted. It reads Arabic, English, and mixed documents, and is tuned for handwritten Arabic invoices and Saudi e-invoice fields.

**Services.** n8n, OpenAI GPT-4.1 Vision, PDF Extract, Validation, Deduplication, Webhooks

- Rejects any file that is not a genuine invoice, before anything is saved
- Extracts 70+ fields plus line items: vendor, buyer, totals, VAT, dates
- Classifies every line item into per-company expense categories at extraction time
- Refuses politely and explains why when required data is missing — accuracy before speed

**Outcome.** Manual invoice entry disappears entirely; a photo becomes structured accounting data in about ten seconds.

### Telegram Publishing System (2026)

*Content system run from a chat* — Built and tested — 4 n8n workflow(s) — trigger: Telegram message and a scheduler

**Flow.** Telegram command → Allowed chat? → Load post context → Parse intent → State machine → Save post job → Reply in chat → Review and publish scheduler → Content generator → Multi-platform publisher

Plan, review, approve and publish posts to LinkedIn, Instagram and Reddit from a Telegram chat. The AI only understands what you meant; every decision after that is made by a deterministic state machine.

**Services.** n8n, OpenAI, Telegram, LinkedIn, Instagram, Reddit, n8n Data Tables

- Button presses skip the AI and go straight to the state machine
- Only allow-listed chats are processed
- The scheduler locks an approved post before publishing, so nothing goes out twice
- Jobs stuck too long are marked failed, with a retry button

**Outcome.** A content calendar that lives in a chat, with a human approving every post.

### Unified Inbox (2026)

*Inbox with AI triage* — Built and tested — 3 n8n workflow(s) — trigger: Incoming message, webhook and schedule

**Flow.** Telegram inbound → New message hook → Outbox poll → Atomic ingest → Worth a model call? → Send via Telegram → Dialect-aware enrichment → Classify locally → Record send result → Save enrichment

Messages from every channel land in one inbox. Each one is enriched with its dialect, intent, priority and a summary, plus a draft reply written in the sender's own dialect — and replies leave through an outbox that records every result.

**Services.** n8n, OpenAI, Supabase, Telegram, Structured outputs

- Greetings and emoji-only messages never reach the model — they are classified locally to save cost
- Every channel is normalised to one contract and written with a single atomic call
- Enrichment continues on error, so no message is ever lost
- The outbox sends one message at a time and records a readable failure reason

**Outcome.** A team answers every customer from one place, starting from a draft that already sounds like them.

### Google Review Reply Manager (2026)

*Review management for shops* — Built and tested — 2 n8n workflow(s) — trigger: Schedule and a Telegram button

**Flow.** Review poll → Fetch new reviews → Draft reply → Positive review? → Auto-post reply → Ask owner approval → Approval button tap → Approve or skip? → Post approved reply → Mark as skipped

New Google reviews are picked up on a schedule and answered in the reviewer's own language. Happy reviews get a reply on their own; unhappy ones go to the owner on Telegram, who approves or skips with one tap.

**Services.** n8n, OpenAI, Google Business Profile, Telegram, n8n Data Tables

- Reviews already answered or already tracked are skipped
- High ratings are posted automatically; low ratings wait for the owner
- The owner's tap posts the stored draft and edits the message to confirm
- A one-off helper fetches each new client's account and location

**Outcome.** Every review gets an answer, and the owner only spends time on the ones that need them.

### AI Job-Match Pipeline (2026)

*Scheduled agent with human-in-the-loop* — Live — 3 n8n workflow(s) — trigger: Daily schedule

**Flow.** Daily job search → Search job boards → Keep new jobs → AI fit scoring → Save to table → High score? → Has apply email? → Approve on Telegram → Manual apply alert → Send application email

A scheduled pipeline that runs five daily search queries across LinkedIn, Indeed, and Glassdoor, scores each role's fit from one to ten with a structured-JSON LLM evaluator, and delivers only the high scorers.

**Services.** n8n, JSearch API, OpenAI GPT-4.1, n8n Data Tables, Telegram, Gmail

- Structured-JSON evaluator scoring fit on a 1–10 scale
- Deduplication against n8n Data Tables so nothing is seen twice
- Telegram delivery of high-scoring matches only
- Human-in-the-loop approval before any application is sent
- Semi-automated applications with tailored AI-generated cover letters via Gmail
- A factory clones the search into a separate daily bot for each user, through the n8n API — automation that builds automation

**Outcome.** Daily job hunting collapses into reviewing a short, pre-scored shortlist.

### Transfer Receipt Check (2026)

*Payment check for registrations* — Running for a client — 1 n8n workflow(s) — trigger: Webhook (receipt upload)

**Flow.** Receipt upload → Check the request → Request allowed? → Read receipt with vision → Shape the reply → Model failed → Send the reply

Behind a chess club's tournament registration: the uploaded bank-transfer receipt is read by a vision model, which also says whether it is a transfer at all. The site applies the rules; the workflow only reads.

**Services.** n8n, OpenAI GPT-4.1 Vision, Webhooks

- Secret, contract version and image size are checked before any model call
- Model failures take their own branch, so the site always gets a JSON answer
- Successful runs are not stored, because receipts carry personal data

**Outcome.** Registrations are confirmed without anyone opening a receipt by hand.

### WhatsApp Group from a Spreadsheet (2026)

*Form-driven messaging tool* — Built and tested — 1 n8n workflow(s) — trigger: Form (file upload)

**Flow.** Contacts upload form → Read the spreadsheet → Normalize phone numbers → Create WhatsApp group → Batch the contacts → Add participants → Find members not added → Send invite link

Upload an Excel or CSV of contacts and a group name: the group is created, everyone is added in throttled batches, and anyone WhatsApp refuses to add receives the invite link instead.

**Services.** n8n, Whapi.Cloud, Excel, CSV

- Phone columns are detected automatically, normalised and de-duplicated
- Members are added in batches with a pause between them, to stay under spam limits
- Whoever could not be added gets the invite link, one message at a time

**Outcome.** A list in a spreadsheet becomes a working group in minutes.

*Data quality pipeline · proof of concept* — Built and tested — trigger: Webhook or schedule

Incoming CRM leads arrive scattered — duplicates, malformed emails, missing fields — and cost sales teams hours of manual triage. This pipeline cleans them automatically and reports on what it did.

**Services.** n8n, Email validation, Google Sheets

- Removes duplicates and validates email addresses

- Splits results into Clean and Rejected, with a reason on every rejection
- Produces a quality summary after each run

## Frequently asked

**What does Nour Aldeen Tofi do?**

He is an AI Automation Engineer and Frontend Developer based in Al Khobar, Saudi Arabia. He designs and operates production n8n workflows that connect language models to real systems, and builds the React and TypeScript interfaces on top of them. He also works as a Software Engineering Supervisor, leading frontend development and owning delivery end to end.

**What is Smart Scanner?**

Smart Scanner is an Arabic-first AI invoice management product. An employee photographs a receipt; an n8n pipeline verifies it is a genuine invoice, extracts every field with GPT Vision in Arabic and English, and classifies each expense. Accountants then review, approve or reject, comment, and export through role-based dashboards. Nour built the entire AI automation engine and the complete frontend.

**Does he work in Arabic?**

Arabic is his native language and it is a core part of his technical specialisation. He builds Arabic-default bilingual interfaces with full right-to-left support, and his document AI pipelines are tuned specifically for Arabic invoices, including handwritten ones and Saudi e-invoice fields — a case most global tools handle poorly or not at all.

**Is he open to work?**

Yes. He is open to opportunities in Saudi Arabia and remotely, on-site, hybrid, or fully remote, and takes on freelance automation and frontend projects. The fastest way to reach him is email.

**What is his automation stack?**

n8n for orchestration; the OpenAI API including GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 Vision with structured JSON outputs; AI agents with custom tool-calling; webhooks and REST integrations; Google Sheets, Google Drive, MySQL, and Telegram as data and delivery layers; and the Model Context Protocol for connecting models to real tools.

**How do I contact him?**

By email at nouraldeentofi@gmail.com, or through LinkedIn. This site also publishes a machine-readable profile and an MCP server, so an AI assistant can look up his experience and projects directly.
